cheat.catalogHelp: Inspect every definition and choose which calls the agent receives. Individual selections are saved while the master switch is off. Disabled calls are excluded from model requests and discovery, and stale calls are blocked. Changes apply before the next model request; work already dispatched cannot be undone.
cheat.promptHelp: This is the exact Cheat Engineering text added to eligible build-agent system prompts. The enabled-call list updates with your selections. Enabled tools execute directly without per-call manual approval.
cheat.promptInactive: No Cheat Engineering text or tool definitions are sent while the section is off, unsupported, or all calls are deselected. Plan mode does not receive this tool family.
cheat.title: Cheat Engineering Tools
cheat.sourceNotice: Downloads save commit-pinned upstream source ZIPs locally. Nothing is extracted, built, installed or executed. Recorded SHA-256 values identify received bytes; they are not independent signature verification. Downloading does not enable tools or authorize process access.
cheat.calls: Available Native Tool Calls and Limits

products.reclass: Preferred structure workflow. Native tools can inspect .rcnet ZIP/Data.xml declarations without running ReClass.NET. Layout resolution, custom nodes, code generation and a live plugin bridge are not implemented. Upstream is MIT licensed; its dependencies have separate terms.
products.cheatEngine: Reference source only, not a connected provider. Native reads, scans and controlled patches use an original Windows API helper, not Cheat Engine code. Review upstream licensing before building, redistributing or creating derivative integrations.
products.debuggers: x64dbg and IDA Pro remain external tools, not connected providers. IDA requires an appropriate vendor license. Existing REA remains available for static analysis.

cheat.directOverview: Direct native Windows memory and DLL tools. Enabling this section allows writes and DLL execution without per-change approval.
cheat.directAccess: List and inspect processes, read and write memory, search byte patterns, follow pointer chains, inspect ReClass projects and DLLs, build DLLs and load them directly. No pending requests, approval IDs or two-minute expiry. Select the intended process before using tools. Only use software you own or are authorized to test.
cheat.runtimeBoundaries: Enabled calls run with Roxy's Windows user permissions, not unlimited or kernel access. Windows access checks, native x64 DLL loading, local-path validation and per-call resource budgets still apply. Reads/writes: 64 KiB per call; scans: 16 MiB and 512 matches; DLL files: 64 MiB. Page larger ranges across calls. No protection changes, privilege escalation, stealth, automatic DLL unload or rollback. Cancellation can leave writes committed or DLL execution running.

engineering.description: Native analysis for shipped applications, binaries, Android, and saved captures. Off by default. No REA MCP server or agent registration is needed.

descriptions.rea: Inspect archives, JavaScript/Electron, .NET, Go, Rust, Flutter, SQLite, PE resources, and saved web captures. Retain evidence and compare findings.
descriptions.ghidra: Decompile native binaries, inspect assembly, follow references, and build function dossiers.
descriptions.jadx: Inspect Android APK classes, decompile methods, and trace references.
descriptions.adb: Inspect authorized Android devices, collect logs and APKs, and perform explicitly requested device actions.
descriptions.frida: Attach to or spawn authorized processes and load instrumentation scripts.
descriptions.wireshark: Analyze saved packet captures with TShark and capinfos. No live capture is enabled.

dependencies.rea: Includes private Node 24.18.0 and REA 6.7.0. Your system Node is unchanged. Linux requires procps-compatible ps on PATH. REA and third-party license notices remain in its installed package.
dependencies.ghidra: Includes Ghidra 12.1.4, shared private JDK 21, and REA. Automatic installation supports Windows x64 and Linux x64.
dependencies.jadx: Includes the compatible headless JADX 0.7.1 adapter, shared private JDK 21, and REA. Its owned Java helper uses the upstream protocol internally, not a registered REA MCP service.
dependencies.adb: Includes Android Platform-Tools 37.0.1 and REA. You must still authorize the device and enable USB debugging. No emulator or Android SDK is installed.
dependencies.frida: Installs Frida 17.23.2's native Node binding. Remote devices may require a matching Frida server installed separately. Only the Frida installation script is allowed to run.
dependencies.wireshark: Uses winget on Windows or apt with polkit on Linux. Saved-capture summaries support Windows and Linux; field-level analysis is Linux-only. Wireshark is installed system-wide, not privately.

engineering.lifecycleBody: Prompt and catalog changes apply on the next chat turn. Disabling is enforced at dispatch immediately. Switching tools and prompt guidance off closes active analysis sessions without uninstalling dependencies. Each chat and delegate has its own target and evidence. Idle workers close after 30 minutes. Export important evidence first. Runtime tools can execute programs or modify authorized devices; only use them on targets you are permitted to examine. Commercial engines and device-side servers are not included.

workstreams.heading: Workstreams
workstreams.autoTitle: New sessions get their own workstream
workstreams.freshTitle: Auto-reset new workstreams to remote main
workstreams.setupDescription: Optional shell command to run in each newly created worktree, across all projects. Leave empty to run nothing. Runs in the background without waiting for it to finish.
workstreams.setupFootnote: Only runs for new worktrees, never when attaching to an existing one. Available environment variables: ROXY_PROJECT_ROOT, ROXY_WORKTREE_PATH and ROXY_PORT. Clearing and saving disables future runs; it does not stop commands already running.
workstreams.freshDescription: Power-user option. On the first message, fetch origin and start the new workstream exactly at origin/main (or the repository's default branch). If the remote cannot be refreshed, the session waits for you to retry instead of using stale code.
workstreams.freshFootnote: Off by default. Only applies to new workstreams, not sessions in the project folder, forks, selected branches, or existing workstreams. Your project folder and other sessions are never reset.
workstreams.autoDescription: Each session works in its own git worktree on its own branch, so parallel sessions can't overwrite each other or fight with your editor. The folder is created on the session's first message, and only in git repositories. Turn this off to run new sessions directly in the project folder.
workstreams.prefixDescription: New workstreams get a branch named after the session. This is what goes in front of it — use your initials, wip, or clear it for no prefix at all.
workstreams.prefixFootnote: Only affects new workstreams. Existing branches keep their names — rename one from the bar under the composer.

browser.title: Roxy browser
browser.description: Opens a persistent browser the agent shares. Sign in to sites here once — your session (cookies/logins) is saved, so the agent can act with your access.
browser.cookiesDescription: Read, edit, import and delete the browser's cookies — the built-in equivalent of the Cookie-Editor extension. Import and export use its JSON format, so a blob copied out of Chrome pastes straight in. To work on just one site, use the cookie button in the browser's own toolbar.

backup.heading: Backup & restore
backup.title: Skills & MCP servers
backup.description: Export your global skills and MCP server configs to a single file, then import it on another computer to set it up the same way. Importing overwrites skills/servers that share a name.
backup.warning: Heads up: the file includes any MCP secrets (headers/env) in plain text — keep it private.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.title: Send anonymous usage data
privacy.description: Counts and timings — app launches, finished turns, how many steps and tools a turn took, how many tokens it used and roughly what it cost — tied to a random id generated on this machine. Never your prompts, your code, file paths, repo names, or any error text.
privacy.labels: A few labels ride along, and each is matched against a fixed list built into the app: which provider served a turn (a custom endpoint is only ever recorded as “other”), which model family ran (“claude-sonnet”, never the exact model id), which built-in tools ran (an MCP server's own name is only ever recorded as “mcp”), and which kind of error ended a failed turn. It is the only way we can tell whether a release helped or broke things.

themes.title: Themes
themes.subtitle: Choose your colors, add a background, and make Roxy yours. Pick a theme below or duplicate one to customize it. Your background stays with you when you switch themes.
themes.emptyLead: No custom themes yet. Duplicate one above to get a file you can edit, or drop a
themes.reappliesHint: Saving re-applies the theme if it’s the active one.
themes.buildWithAiBody: Copies a full spec of this format — every token, what it paints, the rules and a worked example. Paste it into any model, describe the theme you want, and drop the JSON it returns into the editor.
themes.colorsBody: Any CSS color — hex, rgb(), oklch(), or a color-mix(). Anything you leave out is inherited from the theme you extends, so a theme can be three lines long.
themes.fontsBody: sans is the UI font and mono is the code font — tool calls, terminal output, diffs and code blocks. Give one family, an array to build your own stack, or "system" for the platform’s native font. Fallbacks are appended automatically, so naming a font you don’t have degrades gracefully.
themes.swatchesLocked: Save or discard your JSON edits to pick colors here.
